description: Readers respond to an article by Andy Burnham in which he says that people today can’t be held personally liable for the country’s historical wrongs In his opinion piece ( 30 October ), Andy Burnham argues that British people today cannot be held liable for historical wrongs “in which they played no personal part”. On one level, he is right. But he confuses two very different things: personal liability and the continuing responsibility of the state. When slavery was abolished in the British empire in 1833, the government borrowed £20m – an extraordinary sum then – to compensate enslavers for the loss of their supposed property. Some 40,000 claims were made. The British taxpayer carried the cost, and the resulting public debt was not finally cleared until 2015.

This, in my humble opinion, is a problem. Thucydides noted about Pericles, the Athenian statesman, that “it was he who led them [the people], rather than they who led him”. It was arguably the constant and thoughtful guidance of Pericles to his fellow Athenian citizens that made Athens the dominant political and economic power, respected by its friends and enemies alike. Burnham needs to take the lead and show his cards on what type of relationship he wants to pursue with our European partners. Italy’s Matteo Salvini, Jordan Bardella from France, Jimmie Åkesson from the Sweden Democrats, and Tom Van Grieken from Belgium’s Vlaams Belang all led the youth wing of the parties they now run. description: Millions of Americans will gain an hour of sleep this weekend when the twice-a-year time change commonly known as daylight savings ends for 2026. Most of the U.S. will "fall back" an hour when the clocks change at 2 a.m. on Sunday. Here's what to know about what's formally known as daylight saving time as it ends for the year: What is daylight saving time, and why do we have it? Daylight saving time is the period during the year, from March to early November, when the majority of the U.S. operates one hour ahead of standard time. The move effectively "saves" an hour of daylight from the morning and adds it to the evening during the spring and summer months when the days are the longest. In the fall and winter months, when the days are shorter, the U.S. returns to standard time, with daylight coming earlier in the morning. description: For Westminster’s special budget edition of the series, politicians have played to their strengths. Bombast, duplicity, distrust: it’s all second nature You join us on a steam train in Scotland as we head to the next episode of the BBC’s hit show Political Traitors. It’s like the celebrity edition, except that everyone is less comely – politics being the practice of show business for ugly people . For this week’s task, the players have to construct a “budget” of tiny crowd-pleasing measures, carefully balanced by invisible tax rises. What makes the show so compelling is that the players don’t know the whole story. Only those of us on the outside can see what’s really going on. While John and Andy run around shouting about how they have faithfully met their “fiscal rules” in the third year of the forecasts, on our sofas at home we know that this incantation is entirely meaningless. description: Lyn Dade and Lyn Collins respond to an article by John Humphrys about the 1966 disaster and the lessons that haven’t be learned John Humphrys’ righteous anger at the carelessness of national institutions and the horrors that followed as a result – at Aberfan, Hillsborough, Grenfell and during Covid – is matched only by his disgust at the lack of accountability afterwards ( At Aberfan, I saw fathers digging for their missing children. And the lessons society should have learned, it hasn’t, 24 October ). Sadly, it is too often true that those in leadership roles walk away with no more than a slapped wrist. In France, citizens would be manning the barricades. Here? “Dreadful, isn’t it?” Followed by a shrug. Like Humphrys, we should be raging at the death, grief and lasting trauma that were delivered by our “leaders”. But we don’t. Because we don’t believe that it will make any difference. We are apathetic, maybe because we have so little self-agency.

description: Three people are dead after two helicopters collided in midair near an Oregon airport on Thursday, according to local authorities.
